newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Greens leader lampoons Waigel, gold grab.
newsitem.headline: German Greens leader lampoons Waigel, gold grab.

text.p: Joschka Fischer, the Greens leader who ranks as one of Bonn's funniest speakers, had the German parliament roaring with laughter on Wednesday as he lashed out at Finance Minister Theo Waigel's attempted grab for gold.

"You don't deserve the Bundesbank's gold, but a gold medal for creative accounting," declared Fischer, speaking after Waigel roundly defended an agreement he made with Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer to get extra bank profits next year.
Waigel failed to get the bank to agree to revalue its gold reserves to pay out extra profits this year to fill its budget gaps and qualify for Europe's monetary union (EMU).
Fischer also lampooned Waigel's repeated declarations that Germany would still meet the Maastricht treaty's three percent deficit-to-GDP target precisely and on time.
"I can still hear it ringing in my ears - 3.00 percent means 3.00 percent," he said, quoting an oft-repeated Waigel statement. "Now all that is left are the two zeros..."
